objective: Choose a trigonometric ratio to solve a right triangle and interpret the solution with the correct reference angle and units.

sources.title: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, 7.2 Right Triangle Trigonometry
sources.use: Scope and optional reading. Instruction, examples, questions and diagrams are original.

instructionOutline: Identify the right angle before naming sides
Change the reference angle without changing the triangle
Use similarity to explain invariant ratios
Define sine, cosine and tangent
Check the range and units of a ratio
Relate complementary acute angles
Derive the 45-45-90 triangle
Derive the 30-60-90 triangle
Build exact special-angle values
Choose a ratio from the known and unknown sides
Solve for a numerator or a denominator
Recover an acute angle with an inverse function
Keep calculator mode and output units consistent
Solve a complete triangle and retain precision
Model elevation from a horizontal baseline
Include observer height
Interpret depression using parallel horizontals
Separate horizontal run, vertical rise and sloping length
Normalize length units before forming ratios
Audit assumptions and communicate a defensible result
checkpointRule: All four questions are critical and must be correct independently. A four-question form samples four families, not every one of the 35 named practice variants.

conventions.geometry: ABC has its right angle at A. BC is always the hypotenuse. The chosen acute reference angle is at B or C.
conventions.domain: Positive nondegenerate right triangles only; the reference angle is strictly between 0 and 90 degrees.
conventions.exact: Special-angle values and exact lengths accept equivalent rational and radical expressions. Rounded decimals do not replace irrational exact answers.
conventions.approximate: Measured side answers are accepted within 0.005 of the displayed unit and measured angle answers within 0.05 degree, with zero relative tolerance. Retain intermediate precision.
conventions.units: Convert lengths to a common unit before taking a ratio. Ratios are dimensionless; sides and inverse-function angles carry explicitly stated units.
conventions.inverse: Inverse sine, cosine and tangent return acute angles here. They are not reciprocals.
conventions.scope: Full unit-circle coordinates, all six functions, general inverse-function domains and non-right-triangle laws belong to later lessons.

investigation.workflow: Predict opposite and adjacent labels, solve exact ratios and a scaled side, then compare a diagram and accessible table for both acute angles and explain similarity.
investigation.inputs: Exact positive AB, AC and BC with a verified Pythagorean relation; reference angle B or C; positive rational scale.
investigation.validation: Reject nonreal, zero, negative, non-right and out-of-range inputs. Clear predictions, calculations and explanations after any input changes. Reset the selected case.
investigation.evidence: Guided work awards no independent objective evidence.

misconceptions: Calling a leg opposite without specifying an angle
Treating the hypotenuse as the adjacent leg
Swapping a ratio with its reciprocal
Assuming similar triangles have equal side lengths
Adding a degree number to a radian number
Multiplying instead of dividing when the unknown is in the denominator
Treating inverse sine as reciprocal sine
Using a sloping distance as horizontal run
Omitting eye height or measuring depression from vertical
Rounding an intermediate side before the final computation
Using right-triangle ratios without establishing perpendicular legs
